body.x: Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering the convergence of subculture and technology, chose MIRAEROBOT, HD Hyundai Robotics Co., Ltd. and U&S Networks as its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech Into Reality," the third edition combined the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo (DIFA), the Daegu Robot Expo (ROBEX), the ICT Convergence Expo Korea (ITCE) and start-up programs. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

Otaku Soken covers entertainment such as anime and games along with technology and business and economics. Its coverage ranges from hardware for immersive content, including gaming devices, smart glasses and extended reality (XR), to industrial uses of generative AI. It also looks at how original ideas become products and how they affect culture and industry, in addition to a technology's functions.

Otaku Soken joined FIX 2026 as a global media partner for the first time. Yoshioka Tomomi, its editor-in-chief, said he wanted to see trends in Korea's technology market on site and the potential of original hardware and AI technology. He said he was particularly interested in new gadgets that surprise consumers, gaming devices, and fields where technology meets content, such as augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR).

body.x: The three companies Otaku Soken chose cover robot technology for education and research and development, industrial robots for manufacturing, and medical ICT solutions for hospital work efficiency and patient safety.
MIRAEROBOT Supplies Educational Robots, AI Manipulators and Parts

MIRAEROBOT supplies robots and parts for education and research and development. Its lineup ranges from educational robots and coding kits to an AI Worker, AI manipulators, robot kits and parts, and aviation science products. It supports robot building and AI learning in classrooms, maker activities and professional practice environments.

Educational robots let learners build and program a robot and learn its structure and operating principles. AI manipulators and robot parts can be used to learn how robots move and are controlled or to run experiments in research and development. The lineup covers everything from introductory education to advanced practice and development environments.

body.x: HD Hyundai Robotics Supplies Industrial and Collaborative Robots for Factory Automation

HD Hyundai Robotics Co., Ltd., led by CEO Wansoo Kim, supplies articulated industrial robots for manufacturing processes, collaborative robots, FPD robots for flat panel display manufacturing, and robot controllers and peripheral equipment. Its lineup covers welding, handling, machining and other tasks.

A member of HD Hyundai Group, the company began its robot business in 1984. According to the company, it was the first in Korea to pass 60,000 cumulative industrial robot units produced and holds the top market share in industrial robots in Korea. It also serves customers in automobiles, shipbuilding, construction machinery and electronics through overseas subsidiaries in the Americas, China and Europe.

Industrial robots raise production efficiency and consistency in processes that need repetitive work and precise motion. Collaborative robots suit work environments designed around cooperation with people, and FPD robots transfer and handle panels in display manufacturing. Controllers and peripheral equipment such as positioners connect individual robots to a production line to form an automation system.
The robot industry is moving beyond repeating preset motions toward Physical AI, in which robots recognize their surroundings and work to suit the situation.

body.x: HD Hyundai Robotics planned to bring six exhibits to ROBEX 2026. They include a CADless welding solution, in which a robot and vision sensor scan the actual workpiece and recognize its shape to generate the welding path; a tire handling process using the HDC35, a next-generation collaborative robot built with high rigidity for use in areas such as automobile assembly, machine tending and heavy-load handling; and ArcLift GO, a hand-guided collaborative robot on a movable platform suited to shipbuilding. It also planned a dual-arm robot and a software zone at its booth.

body.x: U&S Networks Offers a Digital Nurse Call and Cloud Electronic Board for Hospitals

U&S Networks Inc. is a medical ICT company that applies mobile and IT technology to hospital work and patient safety. It offers a digital nurse call, a cloud electronic board and a patient safety check solution, along with services and system integration tailored to hospital environments.

The digital nurse call moves patient calls and medical staff responses into a digital environment to support communication and workflow in the hospital. The cloud electronic board delivers waiting status, call information and guidance messages. The patient safety check system supports verification procedures in the hospital so that safety-related work is carried out systematically.

Hospitals need quick responses to patient requests, accurate information sharing among medical staff and confirmation of patient condition and procedures. Mobile and cloud technology can improve information access and work efficiency, and systems can be configured to each hospital's way of operating.

body.x: Three Selections Across Education, Manufacturing and Healthcare

Otaku Soken's top three work in different fields. MIRAEROBOT supplies robots and parts for education and research and development. HD Hyundai Robotics supplies industrial and collaborative robots for manufacturing automation. U&S Networks applies mobile and cloud technology to hospital work and patient safety.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including Otaku Soken. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet for IT, enterprise digital transformation and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report to international audiences on innovative Korean companies in future industries.
